title: StagingWriter tmp dir created as sibling breaks container deployments
description:
StagingWriter (connector/writer.go:37) creates tmpDir by appending '-tmp' to the staging dir path: filepath.Join(stagingDir+"-tmp", connectorName). In container deployments where each directory is a separate volume mount, this creates a sibling directory outside any mounted volume, on the container's read-only rootfs.

**Example:** stagingDir=/data/glovebox/staging (mounted PVC), tmpDir becomes /data/glovebox/staging-tmp (not mounted, read-only rootfs) -> permission denied.

**Fix:** tmpDir should be inside the staging dir, e.g. filepath.Join(stagingDir, ".tmp", connectorName).

**RED:** All connectors crash with 'mkdir /data/glovebox/staging-tmp: permission denied'
**GREEN:** tmpDir is inside the staging volume, connectors start and stage items successfully.
close_reason: Fixed staging-tmp path from stagingDir+'-tmp' to stagingDir+'/.tmp'. Updated all connector tests to skip .tmp directory when iterating staged items. All tests pass except pre-existing teams connector failure.

title: [BUG] glovebox:0.3.0 ingest HTTP listener not starting on port 9091
description: The glovebox Helm chart 0.3.0 adds an 'ingest' port (9091) and a startup probe for it, but the glovebox binary (ghcr.io/leftathome/glovebox:0.3.0) never starts an HTTP listener on 9091. It only listens on 9090 (metrics). The startup probe fails repeatedly ('dial tcp :9091: connection refused'), causing the container to be killed after ~60s. Binary self-reports as 'glovebox v0.1.0' which suggests the image tag may not match the actual binary version. Connectors (RSS) crash with nil StagingWriter because they try to POST to http://glovebox-glovebox-ingest:9091/v1/ingest which has no backing endpoints.
notes: Root cause confirmed: main.go never imports or starts the ingest HTTP server. The internal/ingest package exists with handler.go, handler_test.go, and integration_test.go, but main.go only starts the metrics server (:9090) and the fsnotify watcher. The ingest config is loaded and validated but never acted upon. The Helm chart 0.3.0 adds port 9091 and a startup probe for it, but the binary doesn't serve on that port. Fix: wire internal/ingest.Handler into main.go, start an HTTP server on cfg.Ingest.Port alongside the metrics server.

title: Design authenticated identity and data provenance for connector pipeline
description: Design how authenticated identity flows through the glovebox pipeline. When a connector authenticates to a source (e.g., GitHub with a PAT, IMAP with credentials), the identity context (who authenticated, what scopes/permissions, token type) should be captured and propagated so downstream agents can filter/map based on provenance. Questions to answer: (1) What identity fields belong in staging metadata.json? (e.g., auth_identity, auth_method, auth_scopes, source_account) (2) Should glovebox pass identity through unchanged, validate it, or enrich it? (3) How does this interact with multi-tenant deployments where multiple users' connectors write to the same staging dir? (4) What about unauthenticated sources (RSS) -- do they get a synthetic identity? (5) How do we handle identity for webhook-based connectors where the identity is in the request, not the connector config? (6) Privacy considerations -- should identity be hashed/pseudonymized in audit logs? Output: design spec and implementation plan covering connector library changes, metadata schema changes, and glovebox routing changes.
design:
IDENTITY SCHEMA (new fields in metadata.json / ItemOptions):

identity: {
  account_id: string  -- stable ID of who authenticated (email, username, numeric ID)
  provider: string    -- service name (github, gitlab, imap, etc.)
  auth_method: string -- one of: pat, oauth, api_key, app_password, github_app, none
  scopes: []string    -- optional OAuth scopes / permissions on the token
  tenant: string      -- operator-defined string for multi-tenant routing, set in connector config

tags: map[string]string -- operator-defined key-value pairs, matched via rules (see below)

DESIGN DECISIONS:
1. identity is optional nested object. Unauthenticated sources (RSS) omit or set auth_method=none
2. tenant is config-level, not derived from token. Operator assigns tenants in deployment config
3. Glovebox passes identity through unchanged. Validates structure only (field lengths, no control chars)
4. Audit logs include full identity block, no hashing for v1 (audit log is access-controlled)
5. Both connector-per-user and shared-connector-multi-account models supported

UNIFIED RULES CONFIG (replaces routes):
Config format changes from:
  routes: [{match, destination}]
To:
  rules: [{match, destination, tags}]

Same first-match-wins semantics. Tags and destination resolved from same rule.
Router refactored to RuleMatcher returning MatchResult{Destination, Tags}.
Backward-incompatible change to connector config format (acceptable at v0.1).

TAGS:
- map[string]string, optional per rule
- Stamped on items by StagingWriter at Commit() time
- Glovebox validates key/value lengths, passes through unchanged
- Use cases: team, env, cost_center, priority, project

GLOVEBOX CHANGES:
- Validation: accept and pass through identity + tags fields
- Audit: include both in JSONL log entries
- No interpretation of identity (pure passthrough)
- No identity-based routing in v1 (future bead)

EXISTING CONNECTOR MIGRATION:
- IMAP: identity from IMAP_USERNAME, auth_method=app_password, migrate routes->rules
- RSS: identity with auth_method=none, migrate routes->rules

OUT OF SCOPE:
- Device code flow / interactive auth setup CLI
- Secret store integration
- Identity-based routing in glovebox
- Tag-based quarantine rules

title: Research common authentication patterns for Round 2/3 connectors
description: Research and document the authentication/authorization patterns needed for Round 2 (GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Trello) and Round 3 (LinkedIn, Meta, Bluesky, X) connectors. Cover: OAuth 2.0 flows (authorization code, device code, client credentials), API key/PAT auth, webhook signature verification, token refresh lifecycle, credential storage patterns (env vars vs secret stores vs OAuth token files). Identify which connectors use which patterns. Output: docs/specs/06-connector-auth-patterns.md with a matrix of connectors x auth methods and recommended implementation approach for the connector library.
design:
AUTH PATTERN MATRIX:

| Connector | Primary Auth | Token Refresh? | Webhook Verify | Identity Source |
|-----------|-------------|----------------|----------------|-----------------|
| GitHub | PAT or GitHub App (JWT+installation token) | App: yes (1hr tokens) | HMAC-SHA256 | Token owner / app installation |
| GitLab | PAT or OAuth 2.0 | OAuth: yes | Secret token header | Token owner |
| Jira | API token (basic auth) or OAuth 2.0 (3LO) | OAuth: yes | Shared secret | Atlassian account |
| Trello | API key + token | No (long-lived tokens) | None (callback URL only) | Trello member |
| LinkedIn | OAuth 2.0 (3-legged + PKCE) | Yes (60-day refresh) | N/A (poll only) | LinkedIn member |
| Meta | OAuth 2.0 (Facebook Login) | Yes (long-lived exchange) | App secret HMAC | Facebook/IG user |
| Bluesky | App password or OAuth (DPoP) | DPoP: yes | N/A (firehose) | DID (AT Protocol) |
| X | OAuth 2.0 + PKCE | Yes (2hr access tokens) | CRC challenge (HMAC-SHA256) | X user ID |

COMMON PATTERNS:
- 6/8 need OAuth token refresh -> library-level TokenSource
- 3/8 need webhook HMAC verification -> shared VerifyWebhook helper
- All need identity extraction from auth context

LIBRARY ADDITIONS:
1. TokenSource interface: Token(ctx) (string, error)
   - StaticTokenSource: wraps env var (PAT, API key, app password)
   - RefreshableTokenSource: OAuth2 config + token file, auto-refresh, atomic persist
   - GitHubAppTokenSource: JWT from private key -> installation token
2. WebhookVerifier: VerifyHMAC(payload, signature, secret, algo) bool
3. Token file: JSON in state dir {access_token, refresh_token, token_type, expiry}
4. Device code flow: OUT OF SCOPE for v1, separate future bead

CREDENTIAL MANAGEMENT:
- Secrets (client_secret, private key, API key) from env vars / deployment layer
- Library handles OAuth token lifecycle only (refresh, persist, re-auth detection)
- PermanentError on unrecoverable auth failure (revoked token, expired refresh)

title: Watcher uses metadata.json as readiness gate and retries unseen on failure
description: Fix the staging watcher to handle networked/virtualized mounts (NFS, iSCSI, 9P, virtiofs) where directory contents may not be immediately visible after rename. If metadata.json is missing, skip the item (don't mark seen) so the next poll retries it. (2) Only mark items as seen after the handler returns without error, so transient failures get retried. Exit criteria: watcher only dispatches items with metadata.json present, failed dispatches are retried on next poll, existing tests pass, new test verifying metadata.json gate behavior.

title: Watcher dispatches before staging item is ready across networked/virtualized mounts
description: fsnotify fires on directory creation in staging/ and the watcher dispatches immediately, but on NFS/iSCSI/9P/virtiofs mounts the directory contents (metadata.json, content.raw) may not be visible yet due to client-side attribute caching. The watcher marks the item as seen before the handler succeeds, so failed items are never retried by the watcher. The only retry path is the failed-dir rescan, which also fails if the dir was cleaned up. Root cause: watcher treats directory existence as readiness. Fix: treat metadata.json existence as the readiness signal, and only mark items seen after successful dispatch.

title: Archive delivery ingest endpoint for recognizer-to-glovebox bridge
description:
## Why this issue exists

Recognizer (archiver) needs a way to deliver classified archive subtrees to glovebox over HTTP. Shared-PVC handoff isn't viable in this homelab (the NAS that would host RWX storage is offline), so recognizer is moving to HTTP push.

The existing /v1/ingest endpoint (spec 08) caps content at 64MB per request, sized for connector-scale items (one email, one RSS post). Recognizer's deliveries are archive-scale and routinely exceed 64MB:

- A single Gmail Takeout mbox: currently 12GB on the user's machine
- One recognized subtree from an omnibus Takeout zip (e.g., "Google Photos/2024/") can be many GB
- Individual archive deliverables (single calendar export, single Drive folder snapshot, etc.) range from KB to multiple GB

Recognizer needs glovebox to accept these large per-artifact deliveries so glovebox's per-media-type importers (spec 09 mbox-importer, future spec X for Takeout subtrees, etc.) can do the per-message / per-file work.

## What recognizer needs from glovebox

Glovebox owns the design. These are the requirements from the consumer side:

**Transport requirements**
- HTTP push to glovebox over the cluster network
- One POST per recognized subtree / per delivered artifact
- Multi-GB request body (no 64MB cap)
- Single-shot or chunked, glovebox's choice
- Bearer-token auth even in-cluster (lands spec 10's "external-ingest-auth" promotion from stub)
- Returns 202 + item id on success; 4xx with details on validation/auth failure; 5xx retriable
- Idempotent on a recognizer-supplied artifact identifier (same archive_id + same content sha256 should be safe to retry)

**Metadata recognizer will send** (recognizer's view; glovebox is free to add fields or restructure)
- archive_id: short hash + filename stem, e.g. "abcdef12-takeout-20260411t180338z-13-001"
- archive_filename: original archive name as user delivered it
- subtree_relative_path: path within the unpacked archive, "." for raw-file deliveries like mbox
- media_type: stable identifier ("archive/mbox", "archive/google-takeout-subtree", future "archive/facebook-export-subtree", etc.)
- matcher_id: which recognizer matcher claimed this subtree ("google-takeout/mail", etc.)
- provider: "google", "meta", etc.
- sha256: of the request content bytes
- size_bytes: of the request content bytes
- delivered_by, delivered_at: provenance

**Content recognizer will send**
- For raw-file deliveries (mbox today, .pst probably tomorrow): the file bytes verbatim
- For directory subtrees: streaming tarball of the directory

## What's out of scope (glovebox's design choices)

- Whether this is a new endpoint or a variant of /v1/ingest
- Chunked-transfer vs single-stream vs resumable upload semantics
- How the delivery routes to per-media-type importers (spec 09 etc.)
- Storage location (extend the existing staging PVC vs separate "deliveries" PVC)
- Whether glovebox unpacks tarballs server-side or hands them off as-is

## Operational requirements

- Glovebox staging (or deliveries) PVC must be sized to hold archive deliverables. For reference, recognizer's data PVC is 100Gi and currently holds 4 Takeout zips + a 12GB mbox. 50Gi is the floor; 100Gi safer.
- NetworkPolicy on openclaw namespace must allow ingress from recognizer namespace on the ingest port.
- Spec 10 (external-ingest-auth) needs to be promoted from stub to implemented. Token is delivered to recognizer via ExternalSecret reading from a Vault path the glovebox side names.

## Decision context

Decision point already settled in conversation 2026-05-19: per-leaf-file POST was rejected (thousands of round-trips for one Photos year), and recognizer-parses-and-pushes-per-item was rejected (duplicates spec 09 mbox-importer responsibility). Glovebox grows a new ingestion path sized for whole archive artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Spec written and reviewed (new spec or addendum to 08; glovebox owns)

- [ ] Bearer-token auth enforced (spec 10 promotion)
- [ ] Idempotent on archive_id + sha256
- [ ] Staging/deliveries PVC sized for multi-archive workload (>= 50Gi)
- [ ] NetworkPolicy allowing recognizer namespace ingress
- [ ] Vault path documented for the bearer token; recognizer can read it via ExternalSecret
- [ ] Smoke test: recognizer can deliver the 12GB mbox + at least one multi-GB subtree without 413

title: Centralize headless browser via cluster-local Browserless service
description: Pivot OpenClaw's headless-browser needs from per-consumer Chromium-bundled images to a single cluster-local Browserless service exposing the CDP wss:// endpoint. Consumers connect as thin clients. Multiple consumers planned: Schoology refresher (already shipping with bundled Chromium per spec 06 §12), agent tooling for web search + page summarization, future browser-session connectors (LinkedIn web flow, Meta, etc.), and likely a render-PDF capability. Centralizing means: one place to patch Chrome CVEs, one fleet to monitor, one place to apply stealth/fingerprint workarounds if IdPs start blocking CDP, and ~150 MiB removed from each consumer image.
design:
DESIGN NOTES from the 2026-05-21 conversation:

TOPOLOGY: Single Browserless Deployment + Service in the cluster. Replicas=1 initially; can scale horizontally if contention shows up. Each consumer connects via wss://browserless.glovebox.svc.cluster.local:3000?token=$TOKEN. Token provisioned via Vault + ESO. NetworkPolicy gates which namespaces/pods can reach the service.

CONSUMERS expected at first cut:
1. glovebox-schoology-auth-refresher (already shipped; refactor target).
2. OpenClaw agent tools for web fetching + screenshotting.
3. Future browser-session connectors as they appear.

KEY UPSTREAM CHANGE: schoology-go's auth.Login / LoginWithPassword currently pin a LOCAL Chromium via WithBrowserBinary(path). To use Browserless they need a WithBrowserURL(wss://...) option (or equivalent) that wires go-rod's launcher.MustNewManaged + Browser.ControlURL instead of launcher.Bin. Small PR to schoology-go expected; gates this pivot's value for the refresher.

REFACTOR PATH for the refresher (once schoology-go exposes the hook):
- Strip Chromium + apt install from connectors/schoology-auth-refresher/Dockerfile (back to distroless).
- Drop ROD_BROWSER_PATH wiring in main.go; add BROWSERLESS_URL + BROWSERLESS_TOKEN env vars.
- Refresher CronJob mounts the Browserless token Secret via envFrom.
- spec 06 §12 needs an addendum noting the connection model swap.

NON-GOALS: do NOT build glovebox-side abstraction over CDP; consumers use whatever browser-automation library fits their use case (go-rod for Go, playwright for TS, etc.) as long as it accepts a remote CDP URL.
notes: Decided 2026-05-21 to keep as a tracked discovery bead rather than pausing spec 12 Wave 4/5 to design Browserless first. The refresher ships with bundled Chromium for the first deploy and gets refactored as part of this work once the second consumer (agent tooling) is concrete enough to share design constraints.

notes:
Scope confirmed by Steve on 2026-05-21:

1. AUTH SURFACE: Native Schoology username + password, no MFA. Schoology
   serves a direct login form (no Google/Microsoft SSO redirect). This
   makes headless auth tractable — single POST equivalent via chromedp,
   ~150 lines of Go, no Conditional Access / bot-detection risk on the
   IdP side. The credentials live in Vault and are projected into the
   cluster via ExternalSecret (ESO).

2. TOPOLOGY: Separate Kubernetes Job + CronJob (NOT a sidecar, NOT
   embedded in the connector binary). The fetcher is its own image
   (chromedp + minimal Chrome runtime). A CronJob runs every ~6h to
   refresh proactively; the connector emits an HTTP 401 → triggers a
   one-shot Job to refresh on demand. Both write the refreshed session
   cookie into a Kubernetes Secret that the connector mounts (or that
   ESO syncs back to Vault as the source of truth).

3. STILL TO DECIDE before implementation:
   - Library choice: chromedp (Go-native, lean) vs playwright-go (more
     robust against minor DOM changes). Lean toward chromedp for the
     dep footprint.
   - Trigger plumbing: how the connector signals the Job. Either a tiny
     in-cluster HTTP endpoint that does kubectl-equivalent Job creation,
     or a shared trigger file on a PVC.
   - Token-write path: Secret update via K8s API (needs RBAC) vs Vault
     kv write (ESO refreshes Secret on next pull). Vault is the cleaner
     source-of-truth route since the cluster's secret pipeline is
     Vault → ESO → Secret.
   - Failure modes / lockout safety: backoff policy when login fails N
     times in a row; alert routing.

REQUIRED BEFORE CONNECTOR GOES TO LONG-RUNNING DEPLOY. Next step is to
write either a spec 06 addendum or a new spec 13 covering the fetcher,
THEN break into implementation beads.

The PVC template (charts/glovebox/templates/pvc.yaml) always creates new PVCs for all six volumes (staging, quarantine, audit, failed, agents, shared). There is no way to reference an existing PVC.

title: ClientCredentialsTokenSource for OAuth2 client_credentials grant
description: Add ClientCredentialsTokenSource to the connector library for APIs that use OAuth2 client_credentials grant (no refresh token). Needed for Microsoft Graph app-only access. Same caching/mutex pattern as RefreshableTokenSource but uses grant_type=client_credentials with client_id+client_secret instead of refresh_token. Tokens are short-lived (~1hr), re-authenticated on expiry. EXIT CRITERIA: ClientCredentialsTokenSource type, caches access token, re-auths on expiry, mutex-safe, PermanentError on auth failure, tests with mock OAuth server.
design:
DESIGN:

ClientCredentialsTokenSource implements TokenSource for OAuth2 client_credentials grant.
Unlike RefreshableTokenSource (which manages a refresh_token), this re-authenticates
with client_id + client_secret on every token expiry. No token file needed -- credentials
are static, only the access token is ephemeral.

TYPE:
  type ClientCredentialsTokenSource struct {
      config    ClientCredentialsConfig
      mu        sync.Mutex
      token     string
      expiry    time.Time
  }

  type ClientCredentialsConfig struct {
      ClientID     string
      ClientSecret string
      TokenURL     string   // e.g. https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenant}/oauth2/v2.0/token
      Scopes       []string // e.g. ["https://graph.microsoft.com/.default"]
  }

CONSTRUCTOR:
  func NewClientCredentialsTokenSource(config ClientCredentialsConfig) TokenSource
  -- No file I/O, no startup errors. First Token() call authenticates.

TOKEN() BEHAVIOR:
  1. Lock mutex
  2. If cached token exists and expiry > now + 30s buffer: return cached token
  3. Otherwise: POST to TokenURL with grant_type=client_credentials, client_id,
     client_secret, scope (space-joined)
  4. Parse JSON response: access_token, expires_in, token_type
  5. Cache token + computed expiry
  6. Return token
  7. On HTTP 401 or error response: return PermanentError
  8. Response body capped at 1MB via LimitReader
  9. Uses http.NewRequestWithContext for context cancellation

NO TOKEN FILE:
  Unlike RefreshableTokenSource, no file persistence. The client_id and client_secret
  ARE the durable credentials (provided via env vars). The access token is ephemeral
  and re-obtainable at any time. No crash recovery needed.

DIFFERENCES FROM RefreshableTokenSource:
  - No token file (no stateDir parameter)
  - No refresh_token in the POST body
  - grant_type=client_credentials instead of grant_type=refresh_token
  - scope parameter sent (required by MS identity platform)
  - Constructor never fails (no file to load)
  - First Token() call does the initial auth (lazy)

TESTS (red-green TDD):
  1. First call authenticates via mock server, returns token
  2. Second call within expiry returns cached token (no HTTP call)
  3. Expired token triggers re-auth
  4. 401 response returns PermanentError
  5. Concurrent calls don't double-authenticate (mutex)
  6. Context cancellation respected
  7. Scopes sent as space-joined string in POST body

FILE: connector/token.go (extend existing file) + connector/token_test.go
notes:
REVIEW FINDINGS ADDRESSED:
1. Reuse OAuthConfig instead of new ClientCredentialsConfig (same fields)
2. Constructor validates TokenURL, ClientID, ClientSecret non-empty -- returns error (not PermanentError since this is setup time, not runtime)
3. Error messages must not leak client_id or client_secret
4. Non-200/non-401 responses return transient error (consistent with RefreshableTokenSource)
5. Reuse existing expiryBuffer constant (30s)
6. Additional tests: empty access_token in response, expires_in=0, non-401 error codes, context cancellation
7. Add Section 3.4 to spec 06 when implemented

REVISED DESIGN:
- Type: ClientCredentialsTokenSource (same fields minus token file path)
- Config: reuse OAuthConfig (ClientID, ClientSecret, TokenURL, Scopes)
- Constructor: NewClientCredentialsTokenSource(config OAuthConfig) (TokenSource, error) -- validates required fields
- Everything else unchanged from original design

title: Research auth patterns for Round 4 connectors
description: Document auth patterns for: Arxiv (no auth, public API), Semantic Scholar (API key optional, free tier), Notion (OAuth 2.0 with integration tokens), Google Workspace (OAuth 2.0 with service accounts or user consent, Gmail/Calendar/Drive scopes), Microsoft 365/Graph (OAuth 2.0 with MSAL, delegated vs app permissions), Hacker News (no auth, Firebase API), YouTube Data API (API key for public data, OAuth for user-specific). Output: auth matrix and TokenSource mapping for each.
design:
AUTH MATRIX:
- Arxiv: none, public API, 1req/3s politeness. No TokenSource needed.
- Semantic Scholar: optional API key in x-api-key header. StaticTokenSource. 1req/s unauth, higher with key.
- Notion: internal integration token (StaticTokenSource) or public OAuth (also static -- no refresh tokens issued, long-lived). 3req/s. Requires Notion-Version header.
- Google Workspace: OAuth 2.0 with refresh tokens. RefreshableTokenSource. Generous free quotas. Requires app verification for Gmail (sensitive scope). Service account option for Workspace domains.
- Microsoft Graph: OAuth 2.0 delegated (RefreshableTokenSource) or app-only (client_credentials -- GAP: needs ClientCredentialsTokenSource). IETF rate limit headers already supported by our RateLimiter.
- Hacker News: none, public Firebase API. No TokenSource needed.
- YouTube: API key for public data (StaticTokenSource, placed as query param not header), OAuth for private data (RefreshableTokenSource, same as Google). 10k quota units/day free.

LIBRARY GAPS:
1. ClientCredentialsTokenSource for MS Graph app-only (grant_type=client_credentials, no refresh token)
2. Token placement flexibility: Semantic Scholar uses x-api-key header, YouTube uses ?key= query param. Not a library gap -- connectors handle placement, TokenSource just provides the secret string.

ALL 8 CONNECTORS BUILDABLE with current library + ClientCredentialsTokenSource addition.
close_reason: Auth matrix complete. All 8 connectors buildable. One library gap: ClientCredentialsTokenSource for MS Graph app-only access.

value: When writing Glovebox specs (or any policy-relevant schema docs), if there's potential for naming collision or field ambiguity (e.g., two concepts called 'subject'), make the disambiguation explicit up-front with a terminology subsection, not buried in a followup. Why: privacy-relevant schemas are where ambiguity becomes a footgun — a typo'd tag key could silently leak private data. How to apply: when a rename or collision shows up during design, resolve it by adding a named terminology/glossary block to the spec body, not by leaving 'TBD' or 'see §10' notes; apply the resolution consistently across schema, Go identifiers, JSON tags, code blocks, and examples in the same commit.

Implementation workflow: (1) dispatch agents (2) verify vet+test (3) commit (4) /simplify reviews last commit diff (5) fix findings (6) commit fixes (7) close beads. Order matters: simplify must run AFTER commit so it has a diff to review.

Glovebox has a minimal .gitlab-ci.yml on main (added with spec 11 v0.4.0) that mirrors only vet + go test -race from .github/workflows/ci.yml. The canonical CI remains GitHub Actions for release artifacts (docker, helm, multi-arch binaries, SBOM, attestation). Use the gitlab pipeline as the MR-gate signal when github push is unavailable.

Release workflow: NEVER push a tag until the CI build on main passes. Verify go vet + tests + docker builds are green before tagging. The v0.2.2 incident: test files were committed without source files, tag was pushed before CI ran, resulting in a broken immutable release that required a v0.2.3 follow-up.
